craft_notes: Sthāyin: the blocked regress. Sanskrit-first: saptatriṃśa/aṣṭātriṃśa kept the two stations; na ca anavasthā kept the negation; anavacchinnasvātantryayogino kept the yoga-basis fused; pañcakalāvidhiḥ kept the rule-name as close. Rows: 9 (thirty-seventh/thirty-eighth pair), 1 ('such the five-kalā rule' closes — vidhi verdict), 2 (compound spilling). Close: 'such the five-kalā rule.' Rejected: letting the regress run — killed: na ca anavasthā is the verse's whole point; simplifying the yoga-basis — kept fused (the basis IS the block).

lines: And when taught or contemplated, its station
the thirty-eighth. No anavasthā stands, though:
the thirty-sixth, having transcended every tattva,
l4.sanskrit_cite: tad yadā upadiśyate bhāvyate vā yat tatpratiṣṭhāpadam tat saptatriṃśam tasminn api bhāvyamāne aṣṭātriṃśam na ca anavasthā tasya bhāvyamānasya anavacchinnasvātantryayogino vedyīkaraṇe saptatriṃśa eva paryavasānāt ṣaṭtriṃśaṃ tu sarvatattvottīrṇatayā saṃbhāvyāvacchedam iti pañcakalāvidhiḥ

reads_against.argmap: Why is there no infinite regress? → Contemplation would regress to 37, 38… but anavacchinnasvātantrya-yoga knowing ends at saptatriṃśa — the pañcakalā-vidhi closes the series.
c1_essence: No infinite regress: knowing-making ends in the thirty-seventh itself, the thirty-sixth transcendent-comprehensible — such the five-kalā rule.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta-śānta of a scheme counted (wonder at arithmetic settling)
